subject: Biology
description: Prokaryotes vs eukaryotes, organelle functions, cell theory, cell division

questions.stem: The cell theory was first formulated in 1838-39 by:
questions.explanation: Cell theory — original tenets: (1) all living organisms are composed of cells; (2) cell is the basic unit of life. Schleiden (1838, plants) + Schwann (1839, animals) jointly formulated. Rudolf Virchow (1855) added the THIRD postulate: 'Omnis cellula e cellula' — every cell arises from a pre-existing cell. Robert Hooke first SAW and named 'cells' in 1665 (cork sections). Leeuwenhoek (1670s) described single-celled organisms ('animalcules') in pond water.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The MAJOR difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is that prokaryotes:

options.option_text: Lack a true membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles

questions.explanation: Prokaryotes (bacteria, archaea) — DNA is in a 'nucleoid region', no true nucleus. NO mitochondria, no ER, no Golgi, no chloroplasts. Have ribosomes (smaller — 70S type) and a cell wall (peptidoglycan in bacteria, varied in archaea). Single circular chromosome + plasmids. ~1-10 µm size. Eukaryotes (animals, plants, fungi, protists) — true nucleus + organelles. ~10-100 µm. 80S ribosomes. Multiple linear chromosomes. Reproduction usually involves mitosis / meiosis. Note: mitochondrial + chloroplast ribosomes are 70S — endosymbiotic theory (Margulis).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The 'powerhouse' of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria — site of aerobic respiration. Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + ~36-38 ATP (Krebs cycle in matrix; oxidative phosphorylation in inner membrane via electron transport chain). Have own DNA (mtDNA — circular, like bacteria), 70S ribosomes — endosymbiotic theory: ancestor was a free-living α-proteobacterium engulfed ~1.5 billion years ago. Inherited maternally (egg's mitochondria; sperm's are degraded post-fertilisation). Mitochondrial Eve = MRCA of all living humans via mtDNA.
questions.diagram_hint: Eukaryotic animal cell with labelled organelles — nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, ribosomes, ER (rough/smooth), Golgi, lysosomes, cytoskeleton, cell membrane.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Lysosomes — termed 'suicide bags of the cell' — function in:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes — small membrane-bound vesicles containing ~50 hydrolytic enzymes (acid hydrolases active at pH ~4.5, achieved by H⁺ pumps). Digest waste materials, worn-out organelles (autophagy), foreign matter (after phagocytosis). When the cell is damaged, lysosomes can rupture → digest the entire cell → 'suicide' cell death (autolysis). Lysosomal storage diseases (Tay-Sachs, Pompe) result from missing enzymes. Christian de Duve discovered lysosomes (Nobel 1974).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Plant cells differ from animal cells primarily in possessing:

options.option_text: A cell wall (cellulose) + chloroplasts + a large central vacuole

questions.explanation: Three plant-specific organelles: (1) CELL WALL — rigid, cellulose-based outer layer (animal cells lack); (2) CHLOROPLASTS — site of photosynthesis (chlorophyll a, b); 70S ribosomes; own DNA — endosymbiotic ancestor was a cyanobacterium; (3) LARGE CENTRAL VACUOLE — stores water, ions, sugars; provides turgor pressure (when full → cell becomes 'turgid'; loss → wilting). Animal cells have NO chloroplasts; small/multiple vacuoles; no cell wall — flexible. Both have plasma membrane, nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, ribosomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: MEIOSIS — the special cell division that produces gametes — differs from mitosis in:

options.option_text: Producing 4 haploid daughter cells with halved chromosome number; involves crossing over

questions.explanation: MITOSIS — somatic (body) cells; produces 2 identical diploid daughter cells (2n → 2n + 2n). MEIOSIS — gamete formation (germ cells); produces 4 haploid (n) daughter cells. Two divisions: Meiosis I (reductional, n) — homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis), CROSSING OVER occurs (genetic recombination), then separate to opposite poles. Meiosis II (equational, no halving further) — sister chromatids separate. Meiosis ensures genetic diversity (crossing over + independent assortment of homologues). Mitosis = normal growth/repair; meiosis = sexual reproduction.

questions.stem: The 'protein factories' of the cell are:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes — small (~20 nm), no membrane. Two subunits (large + small) made of rRNA + proteins. Site of TRANSLATION — read mRNA, synthesise polypeptide chain. Free in cytoplasm (proteins for cell's own use) OR attached to rough ER (proteins for secretion / membranes). Eukaryotic ribosomes — 80S (60S + 40S subunits). Prokaryotic, mitochondrial, chloroplast — 70S (50S + 30S). Many antibiotics (streptomycin, tetracycline, erythromycin) target bacterial 70S ribosomes selectively. rRNA is functionally crucial — Nobel 2009 (Ramakrishnan, Steitz, Yonath) for ribosome structure.
